body_md: `unsafe` unlocks five powers: raw pointers, mutable statics, unsafe fns, extern, trait impls. It does **not** disable borrow checker — only those five. Wrap in safe APIs.
hook: unsafe does not turn off safety — it unlocks exactly five things.

quiz.explain: unsafe permits only five specific operations.

takeaway: Unsafe is surgical: five powers, still checked.
trap: Sprinkling unsafe to silence borrows; it cannot fix lifetimes.

body_md: `*const T` reads, `*mut T` writes — no borrow rules, may dangle or be null. Deref only in unsafe. Prefer `NonNull` and `addr_of!` for safer handling.
hook: Pointers with no rules — deref one wrong and it is UB.

quiz.explain: Raw pointers skip borrow checking entirely.
quiz.q: How do raw pointers differ from refs?

takeaway: Raw pointers are unchecked; handle with care.
trap: Creating misaligned or dangling pointer is instant UB on use.

body_md: Call C via `extern "C" { fn f(x: i32); }` and `unsafe { f(1) }`. Own the ABI boundary: validate pointers, lengths, UTF-8. Document safety contracts.
hook: Call any C library from Rust — one block bridges worlds.

quiz.explain: extern declares foreign ABI; call inside unsafe.
quiz.q: How do you call a C function?

takeaway: FFI needs extern declarations plus unsafe calls.
trap: Passing Rust &str as char* without CString causes UB.

body_md: Export Rust to C with `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn`. Use `#[repr(C)]` structs, raw pointers, no generics. Caller must uphold documented invariants.
code:
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b }
hook: Expose Rust to C in one attribute.
output: // compiles: exports C symbol `add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32`

quiz.explain: no_mangle preserves symbol; extern C sets ABI.
quiz.q: How do you export Rust for C callers?

takeaway: Export C ABI with no_mangle and repr(C).
trap: Returning String across FFI leaks; return raw pointer + free fn.

body_md: `#[repr(C)]` fixes layout for FFI: field order guaranteed. Default Rust layout is undefined for optimization. Add `#[repr(C, packed)]` only when protocol demands.
hook: Your struct fields may be reordered — unless you say this.

quiz.q: How do you guarantee FFI struct layout?

trap: Assuming default layout matches C; optimizer may reorder.

body_md: Aliasing rule: no `&mut` overlap with live refs, even in unsafe. Violations are **UB** (Stacked Borrows). Use `addr_of_mut!`, raw copies, `MaybeUninit` correctly.
hook: Even in unsafe, two writers is still illegal — meet aliasing UB.

quiz.q: Can two live &mut to same data coexist in unsafe?

takeaway: Aliasing rules hold even inside unsafe.
trap: Keeping & alive while writing via *mut is UB despite compiling.

body_md: `unsafe impl Send/Sync` asserts thread safety manually. Only when raw pointers or OS handles are truly safe to move/share. Document why with SAFETY comment.
hook: Tell the compiler trust me on threads — and prove it.
output: // compiles: H is Send (explicit); still not Sync

quiz.explain: Manual impl overrides auto-trait negative inference.
quiz.q: How do you mark a raw-pointer type Send?

takeaway: Manual Send/Sync needs proof, not hope.
trap: Impl Sync when interior mutability races; data race is UB.

body_md:
`Pin

` stops values from moving — needed for self-referential futures. `Unpin` (auto) opts out. Use `Box::pin`, `pin!`, never `mem::swap` pinned data.
hook: A value you are forbidden to move — Pin makes it possible.

quiz.explain: Pin guarantees stable address for self-refs.

takeaway: Pin pins values for self-referential safety.
trap: mem::forget tricks or overlapping Pin violate guarantees.

body_md: Uninitialized memory is UB if read. `MaybeUninit<T>` defers init: `assume_init()` only after full write. Use `zeroed()` solely for valid-zero types.
hook: Reading memory before writing is UB — even if it looks fine.

quiz.explain: MaybeUninit tracks init state without UB.
quiz.q: How do you handle deferred initialization safely?

takeaway: MaybeUninit makes uninit explicit and checked.
trap: assume_init before full init is UB; init every field first.

body_md: **Miri** detects UB: aliasing, data races, bad FFI. Run `cargo +nightly miri test`. Slow but catches what tests miss. Gate unsafe PRs on it.
code:
$ rustup +nightly component add miri
$ cargo +nightly miri test
hook: Your unsafe code has UB and tests pass — Miri finds it.
output:
// cargo +nightly miri test
// → test result: ok, no undefined behavior detected

quiz.explain: Miri interprets MIR to catch UB dynamically.

takeaway: Run Miri on all unsafe code paths.
trap: Miri passing once is not proof; cover all unsafe branches.

body_md: Split unsafe: `// SAFETY:` comment states preconditions (aligned, in-bounds, initialized). Safe wrapper validates then calls unsafe core. Reviewers check comment, not code.
hook: One comment format makes unsafe reviewable — SAFETY.
output: // compiles: unsafe fn read(p: *const i32) -> i32

quiz.explain: SAFETY docs invariants caller must uphold.
quiz.q: How do you document unsafe preconditions?

takeaway: Document every unsafe block with SAFETY.
trap: Empty safety comment hides missing validation.

body_md: `transmute` reinterprets bits — last resort. Prefer `from_ne_bytes`, `cast`, unions. Sizes must match or it fails. One wrong target type is silent UB.
hook: Reinterpret bits without transmute — there is almost always a safer way.

quiz.q: Safest u32 bits to f32 conversion?

takeaway: Prefer typed bit conversions over transmute.
trap: transmute with mismatched sizes compiles then UBs.

body_md: `static mut` is data-race prone — access only in unsafe, prefer `Atomic*` or `OnceLock`. `static` (immutable) is always safe to share.
hook: Global mutable state without saintly discipline is UB.
takeaway: Avoid static mut; use atomics or OnceLock.
trap: Mutating static mut across threads is data-race UB.

body_md: `extern "C-unwind"` allows panics crossing FFI safely; plain `extern "C"` abort on unwind. Catch with `catch_unwind` at boundary to return error codes.
code:
use std::panic::catch_unwind;
// extern "C-unwind" fn cb() { let _ = catch_unwind(|| {}); }
hook: A panic crossing C is instant UB — unless you use this ABI.
output: // compiles: extern "C-unwind" + catch_unwind contains the panic

quiz.explain: C-unwind permits unwinding through FFI boundary.
quiz.q: Which ABI allows Rust panics through FFI?

takeaway: Use C-unwind plus catch_unwind at FFI edges.
trap: Letting panic escape extern C aborts process.

body_md: Audit unsafe with `cargo geiger`, minimal scopes, no unsafe in public API without wrapper. Fuzz FFI with arbitrary inputs to catch layout bugs early.
hook: Find every unsafe in your dep tree in seconds.
output:
// cargo geiger: counts unsafe expressions per crate
// → drive your crate to 0; audit deps carrying the rest

quiz.explain: geiger counts unsafe usage across crates.
quiz.q: How do you inventory unsafe in dependencies?

takeaway: Minimize and audit unsafe surface continuously.
trap: Hiding unsafe in macros evades review; expand and check.
